cards.summary: AI drafts; humans own the change

prompt.text: What is the safest role for an AI coding assistant?

answer.text: Drafting work that a human reviews and tests.

options: Drafting work that a human reviews and tests
correct: Drafting work that a human reviews and tests

hints: It is a fast assistant, not the accountable owner.

teaching.text: AI lowers the cost of producing code, not the cost of owning it. The fastest safe pattern is draft, review, test, then merge like any other change.

teaching.alt: Colourful lines of source code on a dark screen

cards.summary: AI code passes the same gate

prompt.text: AI-generated code should pass the same

answer.text: AI-generated code should pass the same review gate as human code.

hints: Who wrote the code should not change the rules.
cards.fullLine: AI-generated code should pass the same review gate as human code.

teaching.text: The origin of a diff is not a reason to skip checks. Tests, lint, security scanning and human review apply exactly as before.

teaching.alt: A change opening a gate only after review checks pass

prompt.text: What does GitHub Copilot code review produce by default?

hints: It advises; a person still approves.

teaching.text: Automated review catches patterns such as missing checks or unclear code. It does not take responsibility, so a human approval remains required.

teaching.search: How to automate code reviews and testing with GitHub Copilot
teaching.alt: GitHub showing how Copilot can automate parts of code review and testing

prompt.text: AI often suggests dependencies that look plausible but are

answer.text: AI often suggests dependencies that look plausible but are unvetted.

hints: Nobody checked that the package exists or is safe.
cards.fullLine: AI often suggests dependencies that look plausible but are unvetted.

teaching.text: A model can invent a package name. Verify every new dependency exists, is maintained and is the one you meant before it enters the lockfile.

teaching.search: How Developers Secure AI-Generated Code 5 Security Best Practices IBM
teaching.alt: Five practices for securing code generated with AI assistance

prompt.text: What is the best safety net for fast AI-assisted changes?

answer.text: A test suite that fails when behaviour breaks.

options: A test suite that fails when behaviour breaks
correct: A test suite that fails when behaviour breaks

hints: It must fail for the right reason.

teaching.text: AI can change more code per minute than a person can read. Tests turn that speed into a safe loop only if they genuinely fail when behaviour breaks.

cards.summary: Write the spec before the code

prompt.text: A spec-first workflow writes the intended
before asking the model for code.

answer.text: A spec-first workflow writes the intended behaviour before asking the model for code.

hints: What the code must do, not how.
cards.fullLine: A spec-first workflow writes the intended behaviour before asking the model for code.

teaching.text: A short spec with examples gives the model a target and gives the reviewer a way to judge the result. Without it, both sides guess.

prompt.text: Small diffs are easier to review because each change has one clear

answer.text: Small diffs are easier to review because each change has one clear purpose.

cards.fullLine: Small diffs are easier to review because each change has one clear purpose.

teaching.text: A generated change can be correct and still too large to review. Split it by intent so each diff can be understood, tested and reverted on its own.

cards.summary: Private data stays out of prompts

prompt.text: What should never be pasted into a hosted AI tool without approval?

hints: Assume the prompt leaves your machine.

teaching.text: Prompts may be logged or used under a provider's terms. Keep secrets and personal data out unless the tool and the contract explicitly allow them.

prompt.text: Before shipping generated code, check its

answer.text: Before shipping generated code, check its licence and provenance.

hints: The legal permission attached to it.
cards.fullLine: Before shipping generated code, check its licence and provenance.

teaching.text: A model may reproduce code from its training data. Know your organisation's policy, keep generated snippets small and record where third-party code came from.

prompt.text: The human who merges the change remains

answer.text: The human who merges the change remains accountable for it.

hints: You cannot hand responsibility to a model.
cards.fullLine: The human who merges the change remains accountable for it.

teaching.text: Tools change who types the code, not who answers for the outage. Review, tests and ownership stay with the people who ship.
